text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Friday:

- Swiss Justice Minister Arnold Koller and Swiss President Jean-Pascal Delamuraz presented a draft for a new Swiss constitution. The draft version curtails some civil rights in Switzerland. The number of signatures needed to trigger a referendum has been raised. In 1998, Swiss citizens will have to vote over a definitive implentation of the new consititution.
- The legal affairs committee of the Swiss parliament's upper house approved a bill to investigate the role of Swiss banks during Wold War Two.
- Economic forecasters at Swiss Bank Corp said that they expect 0.5 percent growth of Swiss gross domestic product in 1997. Swiss economy will remain sluggish until 1998.

- Walter Stuerm, who won national fame with a series of sectacular prison break-outs, appealed successfully at the Ministerial Committee of the Council of Europe for having to wait four years in investigative custody until his trial.
- The sharp rise in umemployment in October hit young people more dramatically that older employees. More than 50 percent of people have became unemployed in October were between 20 and 34 years old.
- Swiss metal group Metalor to axe 65 jobs.
